text:
sanjay: FYI customer asked for a single API key that covers all projects under an org for read-only usage (analytics).

rachel: hmm that breaks least-privilege unless we have very tight RBAC layering. why not a service-account + cross-project role?

sanjay: they want simple onboarding for 3rd-party analytics tools — one key per org easier for non-dev admins.

kim: two concerns: permission creep over time, and billing attribution confusion if key is org-scoped.

hao: operationally we already support org-scoped keys, but behavior is inconsistent between Hosted vs Dedicated. Hosted treats org-scoped key as org-root actor; Dedicated maps to project-visible actor that can be restricted.

rachel: that's a problem. we need a clear contract: key scope -> canonical actor -> evaluated roles. If scope=org, policy evaluation should use actor.org_id only, and project context must be explicit.

kim: proposal A: keep current scopes (org/project) but make evaluation deterministic: policies can reference resource.project_id and actor.scope == "org" vs "project". no implicit projection.

hao: Proposal B (longer term): introduce "delegate principals" where an org key can mint short-lived project-specific tokens via a controlled exchange. then analytics can request tokens per-project with limited TTL.

sanjay: B sounds safer but requires token-exchange and audit UI changes. customers may balk at extra integration.

rachel: tradeoffs: A is faster (no infra changes) but we must add guardrails: deny-list specific wildcards, add telemetry, and require explicit opt-in for org-keys that can access projects. B is safer and aligns with least-privilege but higher dev+ops cost.

kim: technical detail: current RBAC engine resolves actor -> principals -> roles. We must ensure role derivation does not implicitly expand org principals into all projects without explicit grant. currently some policy templates do that.

hao: we should audit policies that use "resource.project == actor.org" style templates. scanner could flag pattern matches.

sec-bot: security-scan: 7 policies match risky-implicit-org-expansion patterns. https://ci.internal/scan/4260001111

sanjay: action items: 1) quick audit + list impacted customers (sanjay) 2) add scanner rule + lint (kim) 3) short-term policy contract doc + runtime guardrail (rachel) 4) token-exchange RFC for delegate principals (hao)

rachel: short-term runtime guardrail idea: when a key is org-scoped, require a config boolean org_key_project_access=false by default. if true, require explicit project allowlist. That prevents accidental broad access.

kim: we should add a header-level enforcement mode for proxies: if request arrives with X-Run-As-Project:proj-id and caller is org-key, proxy rejects unless token-exchange happened. example:

  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ORG_KEY_XXX" -H "X-Run-As-Project: proj-123" https://api.redwood.example/query

hao: I like that. Also emit metric api_key_effective_scope {org,project,delegated} and api_key_scope_events counter. need for rollout visibility.

sanjay: timeline? customers asking within week. can we do short audit + guardrail in 2 weeks?

kim: scanner+lint rule in 1 week, guardrail toggle in 2w, RFC for token-exchange in 3w.

rachel: communicate to support and account teams: org-keys may be disabled for cross-project access by default next release. include migration path.

sec-bot: ticket AUTH-4310 created for scanner work https://tickets.internal/AUTH-4310

hao: one more thought: we should avoid retrofitting wildcard API keys into billing attribution. add a header X-Attribution-Project that must be provided and is signed by exchange token to be trusted. otherwise default billing bucket is org-default and customers must opt into cross-project billing.

sanjay: noted. i'll prep customer comms draft after audit. ping me if you need examples of current policies that rely on implicit org expansion.

kim: remembering to tag policy owners in PRs is critical. scanner should auto-create PRs that replace bad patterns with explicit claim checks, e.g., from: resource.owner == actor.org -> to: resource.owner == claim("project_id") AND actor.scope == "project"

rachel: cool. wrap-up: A for short-term with guardrails + telemetry, B long-term token-exchange. owners assigned.

sanjay: thanks all. cc @support @acct-eng in comms doc when ready. :thumbsup:
